answer: A group signature lets any member sign on behalf of the group so verifiers know the signer is a legitimate member but not which one, while a group manager holds a tracing key that can open a signature to reveal the signer if needed. Revocation publishes the revoked member's token so verifiers reject its future signatures without unmasking honest members. A voyage through a canyon of members hides the individual, yet a juniper marker lets the manager prune a bad actor. A farm cannot hide behind group anonymity, because the manager can trace and revoke each fake member once opened.
